name: Community-reported decode throughput for a 70B Q4_K_M served by llama.cpp RPC across three separate machines holding 56GB of VRAM in total
methodology: NOT FULLY SPECIFIED - this is a forum report, not a benchmark. What the reporter states: three machines (one with an RTX 4090, two others each with a 4060 Ti), 56GB VRAM total, llama.cpp RPC backend with a worker on each machine, single request, n_ctx_slot 8192, n_prompt_tokens 649 then 793, output 92 then 163 tokens. Two requests reported: 4.38 tok/s decode (228.56 ms/token) then 3.98 tok/s decode (251.13 ms/token). Per-request, not aggregate - one concurrent request. Prefill was 145.97 tok/s then 37.47 tok/s. Topology, CPU, RAM, llama.cpp build, network medium and GPU split across the three workers are ALL UNSTATED, so this cannot be reproduced.
notes: SINGLE REPORT, one user (u/RazzmatazzReal4129) on r/LocalLLaMA, who posted the full llama-server slot timing logs - which is why it is recorded at all. Do NOT read 4-5 tok/s as an RPC ceiling: the reporter describes this as a first attempt ('I haven't found much online as I was trying to set this up'), the inter-machine network medium is not stated, and a 4090 plus two 4060 Ti split across gigabit ethernet would explain the figure entirely without any RPC-specific penalty. The value is useful as an existence proof that a 70B model can be served in full VRAM across three consumer boxes with no P2P and no NVLink, and as an order-of-magnitude anchor for what general-Ethernet RPC costs - not as a performance figure to plan around.
